narrative:
The model determined that you have a 39% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability crossed the bank's threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the purpose of the loan, and the presence of a co-applicant. Your empty checking account was the single biggest reason for the rejection. Most approved applicants have some money in their account; having none is relatively uncommon and signaled higher risk to the model. The fact that you are financing a new car also pushed the prediction toward denial. While many people finance cars, this purpose was less common among those who were approved. Finally, having a co-applicant on the loan added further concern, as the large majority of successful applicants handle the loan on their own.

Taken together, these three pieces of information outweighed several positive signals, such as your long employment, modest loan amount, and solid credit history of existing paid debts.

You should focus on building a positive checking-account balance over the next few months and consider re-applying for a smaller loan without a co-applicant once your account shows consistent activity. This would directly address the main reasons the model turned you down. (218 words)
